conventions.convention: The balanced model has integers n,m ≥ 1; i indexes biological units and j indexes technical measurements within unit i. All biological effects and technical errors are square-integrable on one probability space, mutually independent, centered, and have common variances σ_b², σ_e² ≥ 0. No Gaussian assumption is imposed.

Treatment contributions are fixed under the conditioned treatment schedule. Under assignment averaging they are random, and their variances and covariances with biological effects and technical errors must be retained.
Biological, randomization, and technical measurement units are distinct design roles. Replicate labels alone do not establish the model's independence assumptions or empirical adequacy.
The example compares averages of five readings under the same fixed treatment, with σ_b² = 4 and σ_e² = 1; its target is the population mean μ + τ.

load_bearing.statement: Y_ij = μ + τ_i + B_i + E_ij on one probability space, with n,m ≥ 1, square-integrable mutually independent biological effects and technical errors, zero means, and common nonnegative variances σ_b² and σ_e². Treatment contributions are fixed for the conditioned schedule; assignment averaging instead uses their declared random joint law.

Under the balanced model, for a fixed treatment schedule, E[Ȳ] = μ + τ̄ and Var(Ȳ) = σ_b²/n + σ_e²/(nm). For a square-integrable random treatment vector under the assignment-averaged law, E[Ȳ] = μ + E[τ̄] and Var(Ȳ) = σ_b²/n + σ_e²/(nm) + Var(τ̄) + 2Cov(τ̄,B̄) + 2Cov(τ̄,Ē). If τ̄ is independent of B̄ and Ē, the treatment contribution is n⁻²Σ_i,k Cov(τ_i,τ_k); if additionally the τ_i are mutually independent with common variance σ_τ², the full variance is σ_b²/n + σ_e²/(nm) + σ_τ²/n.

published_dependencies.used_for: The measurable real random-variable convention for biological effects and technical errors.
Expectation as integration on the common probability space.
Square-integrability, centered-square variance, and centered-product covariance.
Mutual independence of the complete finite biological and technical family, and hence independence of each distinct pair.
Linearity of expectation for the finite averages and their fixed or random treatment contributions.
Finite covariance expansions giving the biological, technical, and assignment contributions to the average's variance.
Factorization of products of independent integrable variables, establishing zero off-diagonal and biological–technical covariances and the stated independent-treatment simplifications.

seams_checked.note: The supplier distinguishes scientific, sampling, assignment, and analysis units and requires an explicit conditioning convention without inferring independence from labels. The replication definition preserves these requirements and adds explicit model assumptions.

The fixed-schedule replication model is a finite linear mixed model: each random-intercept design row selects B_i, technical errors form the residual vector, and a fixed design represents μ + τ_i. Mutual independence supplies independent latent and residual vectors. Zero component variances are permitted, and neither item requires Gaussianity. The assignment-averaged extension is separately stated and retains treatment cross-covariances.
